title: Only registered pest-control products may be recommended in Kenya
farmerLine: Kenyan crop-protection advice has to match a current PCPB registered use and the product label. Ask Mkulima will not name a spray, rate or chemical from memory.
body: The Pest Control Products Board publishes registered pest-control products and registered uses in Kenya. A chat answer must not invent a pesticide. Confirm the crop, pest, registration number and the approved label, including any re-entry or pre-harvest interval, with an extension officer or agrovet.

title: Plant maize after the soil has received moisture, not from a forecast alone
farmerLine: Kenyan maize guidance is to confirm that the topsoil is moist enough before planting. A rain forecast is not enough on its own.
body: Location-specific maize advice in Kenya combines rainfall, soil and crop stage. Farmers should walk the field and check that the seedbed has received enough moisture. A phone forecast can change and does not replace what the soil is doing.

title: Fall armyworm needs scouting; one symptom is not a confirmed diagnosis
farmerLine: Windowed leaves, frass in the funnel or chewed whorls can match fall armyworm and other pests. Scout several plants. Do not spray from a photo or a chat guess.
body: Plantwise-style diagnosis uses several plant parts and field history, not a single symptom. For maize, check the funnel, leaf windows and nearby plants. Management must follow a current Kenyan registered product if a chemical is considered. Ask Mkulima may help you look and locate help. It must not name a spray programme.

title: Serious livestock illness needs a veterinary officer, not a chat dose
farmerLine: If an animal is off feed, suddenly weak, or in pain, contact a veterinary officer. Ask Mkulima will not give a medicine name or a dose.
body: Quality preventive livestock care depends on access to veterinary and paraprofessional services. A phone assistant can help you notice warning signs and find a listed service near the farm. It must not replace a veterinarian or invent an antibiotic, wormer or injection.

title: KAMIS figures are latest reported market prices, not a live shop offer
farmerLine: A Ministry reported price is what was last published for that market and crop. It is not what your buyer or agrovet must charge today.
body: Kenya's Agricultural Market Information System publishes commodity prices by market. Use them as a reference from the farm place. Confirm grade, quantity and the actual offer at the market. Transport cost is usually missing, so a higher distant price may not leave more net income.

title: Daily milk records stay farmer-reported until a visit confirms them
farmerLine: Morning and evening litres should be saved with the date. Added by you is not the same as checked during a farm visit.
body: Dairy decisions get better when morning and evening yields are written down. Ask Mkulima may draft a record from a conversation. It must wait for you to confirm before anything is saved. A later MkulimaCollect count can disagree with a self-reported herd size; both claims should stay visible.

title: Do not invent a DAP, CAN or urea shop price
farmerLine: KAMIS reports crop and some input market figures. It does not replace the bag price at your agrovet. Ask Mkulima will not invent DAP, CAN or urea.
body: If a Ministry fertilizer quote exists near the farm, say so and label it as reported, not a shop offer. If it does not exist, say it is missing. A listed agrovet is not a verified shop unless verification says so. Save the receipt you actually paid.

title: Tomato leaf spots can match several diseases
farmerLine: Spots, yellowing or wilt on tomato can match more than one problem. A single photo is not a confirmed diagnosis.
body: Practical plant-health work compares several plant parts and asks follow-up questions. Photograph the whole plant, both sides of an affected leaf, and the stem. Do not name a definite disease or a spray from one image.

title: Satellite field notes cannot name the cause of a weak patch
farmerLine: A weaker western section on a mapped plot is a reason to walk the field. Satellite data alone cannot say if it is pest, soil, water or something else.
body: Earth observation can show that vegetation is stable or uneven across a mapped farm. It must be combined with the farmer's activity and what they see. Ask Mkulima should not dump NDVI numbers or invent a diagnosis.

title: County extension and listed nearby services beat a generic chat plan
farmerLine: For consequential advice, use county extension, a veterinary officer, or a listed service near the farm. A chat plan is not a farm visit.
body: Ask Mkulima can explain what is on the farmer's record, retrieve published guidance, and point to nearby listed places. It must not pretend to replace extension, a vet, or a PCPB label.
